content: I'll read the test image first to identify the affected plant part and key visual features.
The test image shows a **banana leaf** with multiple oval/elongated dark brown-black lesions scattered across the leaf surface, some with yellowish halos. Now let me check the part index.

Leaf-affecting candidates from our 6 possible classes: **Bunchy_Top**, **Cordana_Leaf_Spot**, **Panama_Disease**, **Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka**. (Anthracnose and Cigar_End_Rot don't affect leaves per index.)

Key features in test image: multiple oval/elongated dark brown-black lesions with possible yellowish halos, scattered across a green leaf. This looks most like Cordana Leaf Spot or Yellow & Black Sigatoka. Let me view the Cordana Leaf Spot reference to compare.

**Analysis:**

The Cordana Leaf Spot reference shows larger, irregular blotchy lesions with orange-yellow halos — somewhat different from the test image.

The test image features:
- **Multiple scattered, smaller oval-to-elongated dark brown/black spots** across the leaf
- **Yellow halos** around the spots
- Spots distributed uniformly across the leaf blade

This pattern (numerous small-to-medium oval spots with yellow margins scattered across the leaf) is more characteristic of **Yellow and Black Sigatoka** (Black Sigatoka / *Mycosphaerella fijiensis*), which typically produces elongated dark streaks/spots initially yellow then turning dark brown/black with yellow borders — matching the test image well. The Cordana reference showed fewer, larger, more irregular blotches, while the test image shows the classic scattered sigatoka-pattern lesions.
